title: Plan artifact readers follow symlinks outside the project boundary

evidence.detail: resolvePlanSessionDir normalizes/path.resolves and only compares lexical prefix, with no physical path check.
Paged artifact reader opens the resolved path with ordinary fs.open, following symlinks.
Prompt artifact reader opens known artifact names through the same lexical directory.
Resume embeds read artifact bodies into agent prompt.
Safe fixture probe confirms a session symlink outside the project is accepted and both readers include outside bytes; see probe log.

trigger: Open a project whose .agents/sessions/<slug> directory, or known PLAN.md artifact, is a symlink to a readable file/directory outside the project, then run /resume-plan <slug> or /plan-artifact <slug> PLAN.md.
consequence: The declared project boundary is bypassed. Resume can send outside file bytes to the configured model without general active-read sensitive-path policy. Private-file disclosure is a conditional consequence of such a target; the audit used harmless fixture text and did not read credentials.
suggestedFix: Resolve and validate physical project/session/artifact paths before reading, reject paths outside intended workspace/session scope, and apply mandatory sensitive-read policy to the actual target. Keep the check coupled to the opened file to address replacement races.
acceptanceProbe: Create a harmless outside file plus session-directory and artifact-file symlinks; prefix read, page read and resume must reject outside targets while ordinary in-project artifacts still work. The existing safe probe currently shows rejection is absent.

title: Prompt-producing slash commands bypass the active bisection admission guard

evidence.detail: Registered command handler returns before ordinary prompt preflight.
Bisection guard is only after registered command dispatch.
sendPromptCommand checks stream/message/chain occupancy but not active bisection.
Mode trailing prompt calls shared helper directly.
Cancelled bisection checks out newest snapshot tree before releasing its lock.
isTurnBisectionRunning=true probe blocks an ordinary prompt and dispatches /mode:default with the same prompt.

trigger: Start /bisect-turn while no agent chain is running, then submit /mode:default <mutating request>, /resume-plan <slug>, /interview <request> or another prompt-producing registered command.
consequence: The CLI admits an agent run while bisection is rewriting the tracked tree. A later snapshot checkout can replace edits from that concurrent run. The probe establishes admission bypass; real destructive concurrent git execution was not performed.
suggestedFix: Put bisection/attachment preflight in the common prompt admission helper or a single lower transaction boundary used by every user, command, picker, action and queue path; preserve bisection stop/list local controls.
acceptanceProbe: With bisection active, table-test every prompt-producing entrypoint and assert no send/queue admission capable of starting a turn; keep /bisect-turn stop/list reachable. After stopping, the same prompt must dispatch normally.

title: Attached TUI validates local providers before invoking its remote backend

evidence.detail: Attach target is recorded before client creation.
Attach mode selects AcpRemoteBackend, leaving inference to live serve.
Provider readiness runs unconditionally for both in-process and attached clients.
No local config/providers returns not-configured failure.
Real hook + ready remote stub + empty local config yields remoteRuns=0 and inline provider-not-configured error.

trigger: Start a configured serve process, then attach from a TUI process that has no local provider config (or whose local routes differ from the server).
consequence: The remote backend never receives the prompt despite being ready; users are told to configure a local provider for server-side execution.
suggestedFix: Make readiness validation backend-owned. Check local provider routing only for in-process execution; expose and consume ACP server/session readiness/allowed models for remote runs.
acceptanceProbe: Use a ready injected ACP backend with empty/unroutable client-local config and assert its run receives the prompt. Keep fail-closed local readiness tests for in-process execution and explicit remote connection/auth errors.

title: Submission drains non-ready file attachments without including or retaining them

evidence.detail: Slash command execution precedes processing attachment check.
Ordinary prompt preflight checks processing status, not failed status.
All pending attachments are drained.
Only ready file attachments enter model context.
Only ready file attachments are preserved for message display.
Initial asynchronous completion updates only current composer attachments, so a drained processing item cannot settle there.
Processing slash-file and ordinary failed-file probes both remove the pending file and send only bare prompt text.

trigger: Select a file and submit a prompt-producing slash command before its async read finishes; or submit an ordinary prompt after a selected file entered error state.
consequence: The model receives no file bytes or failure note and the file disappears from attachment recovery/message display. A late read result cannot restore the removed item. This defeats guaranteed file-menu context at the send boundary.
suggestedFix: Validate all captured attachments at a single admission boundary. Keep processing/failed items in recoverable state until an explicit retry/remove/approved metadata-only disposition; reserve and commit attachment drains only once an accepted send has the intended context.
acceptanceProbe: For ordinary/slash/picker/queued sends, inject processing, ready, failed and metadata-only files. Processing/failed files must remain recoverable with visible status and no silent dispatch; ready/approved metadata captures must carry provenance and matching content exactly once.

title: Client initialization rejection leaves the turn and queue locked

evidence.detail: Send claims chain/queue occupancy before async setup.
getCodebuffClient is awaited outside the run try/finally.
Owner release/safety reset begins only in the later run finally.
Factory can propagate errors; returned promise is not a never-reject contract.
Mounted submit catch appends generic error without releasing send ownership.
Fault-injected client factory rejection preserves chainBusy=true and canQueue=false.

trigger: getCodebuffClient rejects during initialization or lease/backend setup after message preparation.
consequence: UI displays 'Please try again', but retries observe busy occupancy and queue behind a turn that never started. Resetting the conversation or exiting is needed to release this state. A real factory outage was not caused; the failure contract was exercised through its existing seam.
suggestedFix: Wrap the complete owned send transaction, including client creation and streaming setup, in one owner-aware cleanup boundary; release only this send's chain/queue occupancy and retain rejected prompt/context for retry.
acceptanceProbe: Inject a client factory rejection and assert chain/queue locks are released, visible failure is retained, attachments/draft are recoverable and the next normal submit is admitted; keep late-old-failure/new-owner tests passing.

title: Validation exceptions become silent resolved submissions

evidence.detail: Validation catch logs and returns {success:false, errors:[]}.
Empty failure errors intentionally produce an empty validationErrors array.
The failed submission returns void after release, with no user-visible error.
Queue item is removed before sending.
Queue restoration sees only rejected send promises.
Production-shaped empty validation failure returns with user/mode messages but no visibleFailure.

trigger: Local validation unexpectedly throws; the real validator catch converts it to a false result with an empty error list.
consequence: The user's cleared prompt appears in history and then work stops without a reason or retry state. For queued prompts, this resolves as successful processing, so unstarted work does not enter rejection restoration.
suggestedFix: Return a visible sanitized validation failure with nonempty error content and communicate a rejected/not-accepted send outcome to queue ownership. Distinguish preparation/validation rejection from accepted run completion rather than using Promise<void> fulfillment for both.
acceptanceProbe: Inject a validator exception in the mounted send/queue path. Assert visible failure reason, queue/draft/attachments retained or recoverable, no SDK invocation, correct ownership release and successful explicit retry after validator recovery.

title: The 100-message cap discards durable CLI transcript before paging can reach it

evidence.detail: Preparation truncates complete live ChatMessage[] to next.slice(-100).
Load previous only increases visibleMessageCount; it does not read discarded history.
Completion persists currentMessages after this truncation.
Serialization persists the supplied message array rather than retaining older blocks.
Envelope and chat-messages sidecar are updated from the same serialized retained messages.
Model continuation history is a separate RunState field.
105 seeded CLI messages plus preparation retain 100 and remove old-0; model history was not involved.

trigger: Continue a conversation whose CLI transcript exceeds 100 messages (including mode/system/bash rows), then send another prompt and allow it to persist.
consequence: Older visible CLI output and prior tool/agent presentation are removed from live and later saved CLI transcript; paging/searching that transcript cannot reach them. This is a bounded-retention design gap, not evidence of SDK model-history loss: RunState/model history and compaction archive are separate and unchanged by this line.
suggestedFix: Separate rendering/working-set limits from durable transcript retention. Keep a paged archive or explicitly documented retention policy with export/recovery before trimming; do not grow the renderer's hot working set without a measured bound.
acceptanceProbe: After >150 CLI messages and a save/reload, the oldest retained-by-policy message must be accessible through archive paging/export or the UI must explicitly disclose the retention cutoff. Separately assert SDK RunState continuity to prevent conflating the two stores.

title: Live plan list/active-session commands are absent from the advertised command catalog

evidence.detail: Executable registry defines /plans and alias plan-ls.
Executable registry defines /plan-use and plan-active/use-plan aliases.
Static menu lists resume/update/status/artifact/lessons but its complete array has no plans or plan-use entries.
Suggestions are derived from that menu array plus skills/presets.
Command palette is passed the same array.
Docs call the menu array authoritative for every registered command.
Docs advertise /plans and /plan-use as ordinary local controls.

trigger: Search slash suggestions or command palette for the documented plan listing or active-session selection command.
consequence: Functional local controls are unavailable through their ordinary discovery surface; users must know hidden typed command names. Registry and catalog have drifted.
suggestedFix: Add the missing discoverable plan commands and aliases, then derive executable and menu metadata from one command contract with explicit hidden entries rather than maintaining parallel arrays.
acceptanceProbe: Every intended discoverable executable command, including plans/plan-use, must appear in slash suggestions and palette, resolve each alias and retain its real local dispatch behavior; explicitly exempt insertion-only or intentionally hidden commands.

title: AI SDK retry wrappers disable configured failover after initial HTTP 5xx

evidence.detail: Production agent requests set maxRetries: 3, enabling AI SDK transport retries.
streamText spreads streamParams, including that maxRetries value; only OAuth explicitly disables SDK retries at line 1361.
getErrorStatusCode only reads top-level numeric statusCode/status; it does not unwrap AI_RetryError.lastError.
Configured backup requires isFailoverEligibleError(error), which receives the wrapper.
A wrapper with no top-level status is ineligible for failover.
Documented 5xx behavior is retries followed by configured failover.

trigger: An ordinary agent request (maxRetries: 3) receives initial HTTP 503 responses whose message is 'Provider unavailable'; defaultModel=local/primary and failoverModels=['local/backup'].
consequence: Observed actual AI SDK/adapter path makes four primary HTTP requests, throws AI_RetryError with lastError.statusCode=503 but classifierStatus absent, and makes zero backup requests. This is not the intended Openbuff outer retry/failover policy; UI attempt/status telemetry cannot see the inner retries either.
suggestedFix: Choose one retry owner for all provider request paths (prefer the Openbuff loop with AI SDK maxRetries: 0), preserve the last provider error/status in a canonical error contract, and classify failover on that contract.
acceptanceProbe: Use the offline HTTP fixture from evidence/02-providers-probes.test.ts, probe http-retry-wrapper-disables-failover: primary returns HTTP503 + Retry-After:0, backup streams text. Require bounded primary attempts followed by one backup attempt, final success, and accurate retry/failover status events.

title: In-band SSE error status is converted into prose instead of retry metadata

evidence.detail: createOpenAICompatibleStreamError embeds code/status/details into Error.message but only assigns name; it does not retain status/statusCode properties.
The production SSE adapter uses that converter for error chunks.
The stream loop throws that converted Error for non-tool errors.
Retry/failover status extraction only reads numeric properties, not embedded message JSON.
Existing 'preserves structured provider metadata' regression checks message contents rather than retry-classifier-visible status.

trigger: A configured provider opens HTTP200 SSE and emits {error:{message:'Upstream provider failure',code:'upstream_error',status:'503'}} before any content, with a configured backup.
consequence: Observed real SDK stream receives OpenAICompatibleStreamError, classifier status is absent, and performs one primary request with no retry or backup, despite an explicit server-error status in the provider payload.
suggestedFix: Normalize validated numeric/string status into a structured numeric statusCode and preserve provider code/details separately from the display message. Reuse the same error contract as HTTP failures.
acceptanceProbe: Run the sse-status-loss fixture through the production configured model and AI SDK. Require classifier status503 and the documented bounded retry→backup behavior before any content is delivered; malformed status must remain unclassified.

title: Default streaming transport drops usage and suppresses configured cost accounting

evidence.detail: stripProviderMetadata defaults true for OpenAI-compatible providers.
CLI/SDK configured OpenAI-compatible providers use the local OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel.
That production constructor always sets includeUsage: undefined; config exposes no includeUsage control.
The usage request field is sent only when includeUsage is enabled.
On a tool-calls finish, the default adapter terminates the stream before later usage chunks.
Both provider cost extraction and configured-pricing fallback are inside !stripProviderMetadata.
If cost fallback does run without token counts, computeCostCentsFromUsage treats missing usage as zero.
Reported cost is accumulated into step accounting.
The usage callback unconditionally feeds cache totals and token-calibration observations.
The green late-usage test explicitly constructs includeUsage: true, unlike the shipped constructor.

trigger: A real configured OpenAI-compatible stream uses pricing input=$3/M, output=$15/M and offers usage 20,000 input +10,000 output tokens. A tool turn sends usage after finish_reason=tool_calls; separately a normal text turn sends known usage with stripProviderMetadata=true.
consequence: Observed tool stream delivers its tool call but loses all offered usage; with metadata stripping disabled the cost callback reports0 instead of21 cents. With the default stripping flag enabled, a text stream retains usage but never calls the cost observer at all. Cache/calibration inputs and step cost therefore lack truthful provider provenance. Actual provider charges and hard budget enforcement were not measured by these probes.
suggestedFix: Separate request-metadata compatibility from response accounting; negotiate include_usage for supporting endpoints and retain terminal usage when requested; represent unknown usage/cost distinctly from zero. Keep high precision internally and round only for display. Attach provider/model/currency/provenance to accounting.
acceptanceProbe: Use late-tool-usage and strip-provider-metadata-cost-gate fixtures with the real configured adapter. Both must report21 cents with 20k/10k usage, preserve exactly one tool call, and report unknown rather than0 when the endpoint supplies no usage. Test endpoints that reject include_usage via an explicit compatibility control, and assert runtime aggregates receive the same receipt.

title: Context preflight requires backup credentials before a healthy primary can run

evidence.detail: Context resolution is documented as capacity-only without touching credentials.
It scans every primary/failover candidate and calls credential-validating resolveConfiguredProviderModel.
A matched backup with missing apiKeyEnv throws synchronously.
The production agent loop calls the resolver before its first programmatic step.
The stream path also calls it before entering the guarded provider attempt loop.
CLI readiness validates the selected root provider, so the primary can pass readiness before this backup error.
Failover is documented as secondary and starts only after primary request failure.

trigger: defaultModel=local/primary is an unauthenticated local provider with a valid200k window; failoverModels includes backup/emergency with HTTPS endpoint and an unset apiKeyEnv.
consequence: Observed getModelForRequest successfully constructs the primary, but capacity resolution and promptAiSdkStream throw the backup missing-key error before any fetch. A dormant emergency route takes down the otherwise usable primary.
suggestedFix: Resolve route/model capability metadata without credential validation; check credentials when a candidate is actually selected. Surface invalid backup readiness separately, with a defined skip/fail behavior when failover is needed.
acceptanceProbe: Use context-preflight-backup-credential-coupling fixture. Require primary window200k and a successful primary request with backup credentials absent. If primary fails, require a precise backup configuration result without erasing the primary failure.

title: Configured reasoning effort is omitted for custom OpenAI-compatible provider IDs

evidence.detail: Configured route effort is resolved and exposed on ModelResult.
withConfiguredReasoningEffort writes providerOptions.openaiCompatible and providerOptions.openai.
The adapter's providerOptionsName is the configured provider ID.
The generic options namespace read by the adapter is 'openai-compatible' (hyphenated), followed by the provider ID.
reasoning_effort is emitted only from the options it parsed.
Template effort uses the same camelCase namespace, so the generic route shares the mismatch.

trigger: A custom provider ID 'local' declares reasoning support and high/medium/low efforts; defaultReasoningEffort='high'; a normal agent stream is sent through the actual configured adapter.
consequence: Observed ModelResult.reasoningEffort is high while the HTTP body has no reasoning_effort. Providers named 'openai' can use the other namespace, making behavior depend on the arbitrary configuration ID rather than declared capabilities. Adaptive role choices can likewise be selected but never transmitted.
suggestedFix: Publish one canonical generic provider-options namespace and use it consistently at producer/adapter boundaries, or map options using the resolved provider ID. Preserve compatibility with existing public option names and validate effort support.
acceptanceProbe: Use reasoning-provider-options-namespace fixture; run high/medium/low route and template overrides for provider IDs local, custom-gateway, and openai. Require the same correct wire reasoning_effort or an explicit unsupported-setting result.

title: Configured OAuth routes ignore the skip flag used for recovery

evidence.detail: The resolver receives skipChatGptOAuth.
A configured chatgpt-oauth provider is selected unconditionally; skip/rate-limit flags are checked only in the later implicit OAuth branch.
Only implicit OAuth honors skipChatGptOAuth and the rate-limit cache.
The OAuth rate-limit recovery recursively calls the same params with skipChatGptOAuth:true to obtain configured provider fallback.
Failed auth refresh uses the same skip-based fallback.
Non-streaming requests also rely on skipChatGptOAuth:true.
Existing test checks the policy helper's skip behavior, not actual configured model selection.

trigger: defaultModel='codex/gpt-5.5', provider codex type chatgpt-oauth; recovery or a non-streaming caller invokes getModelForRequest with skipChatGptOAuth:true.
consequence: Observed actual model resolver still requests OAuth credentials and returns isChatGptOAuth:true. Thus the recursive recovery path can revisit the same excluded provider instead of selecting BYOK backup. A known configured OAuth rate limit is not prevented by the cache in that branch. The probe injected credentials and did not exercise real refresh/subscription services.
suggestedFix: Define explicit OAuth recovery routing: honor skip for configured routes, select only configured BYOK backup candidates, and fail with an actionable reconnect/route message when none exists. Make rate-limit state apply to configured OAuth routes too.
acceptanceProbe: Use configured-oauth-ignores-skip fixture plus a simulated pre-content429/failed-auth-refresh recovery. After skip is requested, neither OAuth credential getter nor backend fetch may be called again; configured BYOK backup must run or an actionable terminal error must result.

title: Streaming retry bypasses the shared deterministic-error policy

evidence.detail: The shared classifier fails fast for content-policy errors and explicit non-retryable statuses, and extracts bounded Retry-After.
Streaming normalizes content-policy errors but does not call the shared classifier afterward.
Streaming accepts transient message OR retryable status OR empty stream; a policy error retaining503 is consequently retried.
Streaming always computes exponential delay rather than applying the shared Retry-After decision.
Non-streaming uses runWithRetryPolicy, so policies diverge.
The retry matrix tests the correct helper, not the production streaming gate.

trigger: An injected provider stream fails before output with createProviderContentPolicyError({statusCode:503}); the shared classifier says retryable:false.
consequence: Observed promptAiSdkStream makes four stream attempts and three backoff calls while the shared policy requires one. Deterministic refusals can consume extra requests and delay, and the streaming layer does not share the documented header-aware decision. The four attempts are Openbuff outer stream calls in this DI probe; they are distinct from the four internal HTTP retries in02-F1.
suggestedFix: Use classifyRetryableError in the streaming gate, with the explicit no-content and empty-stream exceptions retained. Apply its delayMs and cancellation semantics. Combine with a single retry owner so policy is checked before hidden SDK retries.
acceptanceProbe: Use stream-loop-bypasses-shared-retry-classifier fixture. Require one call/no backoff for policy503 and non-retryable400 containing transient-sounding text; require bounded Retry-After for429, no retry after user abort, and existing safe buffered-tool retry/failover regressions to remain passing.

title: Cost-budget stops reenter missing-output correction without consuming the step cap

evidence.detail: Pre-budget return sets shouldEndTurn=true without hitStepCap or consuming stepsRemaining.
Non-reviewers default to no maximum missing-output retries.
Correction suppresses only hitStepCap stops; it cannot distinguish budget termination.
Correction resets shouldEndTurn=false, causing another pre-budget short circuit.
Existing test explains why step-cap retries must not be resurrected, but covers ordinary provider steps rather than cost stop.
DI probe observed 3 cost-stop messages, 2 correction messages, zero provider calls, and stepsRemaining still 1; only probe-supplied abort ended it.

trigger: Run a prompt-only non-reviewer template with outputSchema, no output, default maxMissingOutputRetries, maxCostCents=0 (or an already exhausted cost cap), and stepsRemaining>0.
consequence: The intended terminal budget stop becomes an unbounded retry cycle with no LLM call and no step consumption. It repeatedly grows/compacts message history and occupies the run until cancellation; a fixed step cap does not bound it.
suggestedFix: Carry a typed terminal reason from runAgentStep through loopAgentSteps and programmatic steps. Treat budget/step/cancellation stops as terminal incomplete outcomes and run schema correction only after model-requested completion; do not merely add another arbitrary retry limit.
acceptanceProbe: Run the provider-free probe setup with one available step, unset output and maxCostCents=0, remove its observation-triggered abort, and assert one budget stop, zero provider calls, bounded messages, a naturally returned incomplete result and no successful terminal marker. Also cover a cap crossed after one real DI provider step and reviewer/non-reviewer variants.

title: Caught handleSteps errors and aborts are journaled and receipted as completed

evidence.detail: Catch sets endTurn=true for all errors, appends an assistant error string and stores output.error.
It returns the normal programmatic result without propagating a failed/cancelled terminal reason.
The caller interprets endTurn as normal shouldEndTurn.
The loop breaks normally on that flag, bypassing failure/abort catch.
Normal exit writes a terminal completed step boundary.
Normal finishAgentRun is status completed.
Without an explicit terminal failure, a non-mutation child defaults to completed.
Supervised successful-loop settlement uses the same runtime receipt derivation.
DI exception probe observed completed finish, terminal completed journal, and completed/ok/errors=[] child receipt; abort probe observed the same successful finish with parent signal aborted.

trigger: A programmatic generator throws, yields an invalid operation, or encounters an execution rejection inside the main runProgrammaticStep catch. A genuine parent abort thrown there follows the same path.
consequence: The error text is visible, but the machine contract says success: journal replay treats the run as cleanly complete and the parent can receive a completed/ok receipt with no errors. A cancellation can likewise be recorded as completed, undermining task continuation and supervision decisions.
suggestedFix: Use an explicit programmatic success/failure/cancellation result or rethrow into the loop terminal handler after preserving current state. The loop must finish as failed/cancelled, preserve pending work, avoid a successful terminal journal marker, and make runtime child receipts derive from that authoritative outcome.
acceptanceProbe: Change the diagnostic exception/abort probes to require failed/cancelled finish statuses, no terminal completed boundary, and child receipts with failed/cancelled status and a typed error. Extend to a rejected awaited tool, partial edits before error, and real supervised bridge settlement; keep an ordinary successful generator control case.

title: Terminal task transitions reuse the start event identity and permanently park V2 turns

evidence.detail: The created->active task.transitioned event uses sourceIndex:1.
The active->terminal task.transitioned event also uses sourceIndex:1 with the same project/session/user-input identity.
Identity hashes project, session, user input, call ID, event type and source index; it excludes time and payload.
The store correctly rejects an existing ID whose contents are not an idempotent match.
Terminal state is marked finishing before append and stays parked on rejection.
Preparation replays a parked terminal before any new retrieval; rejection degrades the turn and returns.

trigger: An ordinary configured V2 turn reaches finishTurn after its startup lifecycle batch committed. The same identity collision occurs for completed, failed and cancelled terminal status.
consequence: The whole terminal batch (query completion/failure, task transition, session end and any usage feedback) rolls back. Restoring that state replays the uncommittable batch, leaves status=finishing and installs no V2 context; subsequent capture readiness is not re-established.
suggestedFix: Give lifecycle start and terminal transitions distinct phase-stable event identities while retaining repeat-terminal idempotency. Add a supported reconciliation strategy for already parked legacy turns; do not weaken SQLite's payload equality check.
acceptanceProbe: Use the real SQLite repository with the coordinator: prepare, capture, finish, close/reopen, restore and prepare the next turn. Completed/failed/cancelled all reach the intended terminal state; re-finishing/replay produces no duplicate and never reuses the start transition's ID. Include repair of a checkpoint parked by the current ID scheme.
observed: Different occurredAt values and active/completed payloads had identical event IDs; rejection was invalid-request/idempotency conflict. Restored preparation remained finishing with lifecycle-append-failed and no context.

title: Production turn preparation filters prior-task memory out of the next decision

evidence.detail: A normal new user input derives a new task ID; only interrupted-turn resume reuses the previous task.
That newly created taskId is supplied as an exact filter on every ordinary retrieval request.
Observation candidates must have the exact requested taskId; there is no ordinary global fact/decision exception.
A correlated V2 context suppresses the V1 compiled message even when the result contains no observations.
The advertised cold-start reuse test queries SQLite directly without taskId, bypassing the production coordinator filter.
An optional configured semantic expander can append cross-task advisory discoveries; it does not fix ordinary lexical retrieval.

trigger: A new CLI/SDK turn or fresh session asks about a path/claim learned in a different V2 task, with no semantic recall expander configured.
consequence: The observation is durable and queryable by the store, but ordinary turn context omits it and reports degradation=none. Fixing persistence alone cannot enable cross-task reuse or outcome-guided learning at the next turn. A mostly empty correlated V2 result also masks available V1 operational memory.
suggestedFix: Separate current-task correlation/ranking boosts from an explicit exact task filter. Perform a bounded project-wide knowledge query for new work, retain scope/freshness filtering, and keep active operational task state available independently.
acceptanceProbe: Through the production coordinator plus real SQLite, learn a public fixture path/decision in turn A, finish, close/reopen and ask relevant turn B. B must inject the applicable prior observation without raw task-ID knowledge; unrelated tasks stay out through relevance policy, not blanket exclusion. Exercise semantic recall disabled/enabled and V1 shadow present/absent.
observed: Cold coordinator injection contained zero observations with degradation none; a correlated query to the same reopened store without taskId returned the prior discovery.
scopeClarification: This is the V2 observation retrieval path. Home/project knowledge files and skill discovery are independent and continue to load. Taskless V2 observations would also fail the exact-task predicate; optional advisory semantic expansion is a separate bypass.

title: Explicit decision capture persists identity metadata but discards the decision and excerpt

evidence.detail: The native handler records the actual kind-prefixed text in V1 task memory.
Successful output explicitly echoes text, evidenceSelectors and optional excerpt.
The coordinator reads echoed text for claim identity/dedup.
Persisted evidence excerpts are synthesized tool/path/count descriptions, not the echoed excerpt.
Canonical observation summary/detail contain only tool name, path counts and output digest; decision text is not copied.
Current capture tests assert kind and selectors, not preservation of the decision's meaning.

trigger: The model calls record_decision with a meaningful decision/rationale and optional evidence excerpt under safe V2 capture.
consequence: Canonical V2 memory and its semantic/lexical projections cannot recall what was decided or why. V1 memory and transcript copies mitigate total loss, but V2 authority cannot independently retain the advertised decision content.
suggestedFix: Persist bounded explicit record_decision text/rationale and its approved excerpt in the canonical observation/evidence fields. Keep generic tool capture minimal; preserve untrusted-evidence framing, path validation and length limits.
acceptanceProbe: Run native record_decision -> SDK capture -> real SQLite export/query -> compiler -> close/reopen. Assert exact rationale and bounded excerpt survive in the intended V2 fields and prompt; test dedup/reinforcement and supersession without relying on V1 import.
observed: Handler success and V1 text retention were true; serialized V2 event contained neither DECISION_SENTINEL nor PUBLIC_EXCERPT_SENTINEL.

title: Later compaction snapshots shadow full-result recall with an archived tombstone

evidence.detail: Eviction archives the original body before replacing message history with tombstones.
The next semantic pass archives that already tombstoned history.
Pre-compaction capture copies tool messages without excluding tombstones.
Exact-ID recall scans all archive kinds newest-first and returns the first matching ID, regardless of body completeness.
The model-visible tool takes this exact-ID path whenever toolCallId is supplied.
Duplicate-ID tests use hand-built eviction snapshots, not eviction followed by pre-compaction capture.

trigger: A stale result is evicted, then a semantic/mechanical pass archives the tombstoned message under the same call ID while its original eviction snapshot remains retained.
consequence: recall_context(toolCallId=...) returns the newer tombstone, often telling the caller to use recall again, instead of the still-stored original. Independent eviction retention caps do not protect selection semantics. Keyword recall can still be a workaround.
suggestedFix: Prefer the original eviction payload for exact-call recovery, or represent original/body-completeness explicitly and skip pointer-only/slimmed copies. Preserve immutable identity and provenance across later snapshots.
acceptanceProbe: Use the real evictor at its default six-step recency threshold, archive its original result, run three pre-compaction captures, persist, close/reopen and call recall_context by ID. Return the original body/provenance before and after reopen; cover slimmed receipts and partial-body copies as well.
observed: Original was recoverable before compaction and remained stored after three snapshots, but exact-ID recall returned a tombstone afterward and after SQLite reopen.

title: Prompt compilation alphabetizes ranked retrieval and clips away the most relevant item

evidence.detail: The repository computes a deterministic relevance/freshness/usefulness ordering for observation candidates.
Semantic additions are deliberately appended after the lexical reusableDiscovery prefix.
Verified categories are sorted by JSON string content before compilation.
Reusable discoveries are likewise sorted by JSON content, losing repository order and advisory tail position.
The root character budget clips the resulting category block from its beginning.
Tests incorrectly treat ranked DTO category arrays as semantically unordered.

trigger: A ranked query result contains enough long items to exceed the compiler's 12,000-character budget, or a semantic advisory item's ID sorts ahead of a lexical match.
consequence: The final model input favors JSON/ID order instead of the retrieval policy. The best relevant constraint may be omitted, while optional semantic recall can reorder/displace the intended lexical prefix.
suggestedFix: Preserve ranked category order; canonicalize only genuinely unordered nested metadata. Budget complete selected items in priority order and return an emitted-observation receipt so usage accounting knows what was actually shown.
acceptanceProbe: Supply a valid ranked DTO with one highest-priority z-ID item followed by eight long low-priority a-ID items. At the production compiler budget, the highest-priority item survives and advisory additions never displace the lexical prefix. Check determinism without declaring rank arrays unordered.
observed: Nine schema-valid discoveries with highest first compiled to exactly 12,000 characters, retained LOW_RELEVANCE_0 and omitted HIGH_RELEVANCE_SENTINEL. Increasing the budget alone made the high item reappear.

title: Verifying an effective playbook removes it from both instruction and gate consumers

evidence.detail: An active enforced rule meeting effectiveness thresholds transitions to verified.
The real operator apply path persists that status through setPlaybookStatus.
Runtime listPlaybooks selects only status=active.
The instruction compiler drops schema-valid verified rows.
The deterministic gate also skips every status except active.
A unit test explicitly locks in disappearance of verified rules.

trigger: An operator applies the lifecycle evaluator's verify transition to a rule whose gate counters demonstrate effectiveness.
consequence: The supposedly successful learned procedure disappears from subsequent load, prompt instruction and gate enforcement, even though it was neither retired nor expired.
suggestedFix: Model verification quality independently from activation, or consistently treat verified as active across repository, compiler and gate consumers. Keep retirement and expiry as the deactivation conditions.
acceptanceProbe: Create/load a rule, record the effectiveness thresholds, apply the actual verify transition, close/reopen and reload. It stays present and still gates the same action, while retired/expired rules remain absent.
observed: The real lifecycle returned verify; after persistence status was verified, gate-facing row count dropped from two to one and compiling the verified row returned zero characters.

title: Usage feedback labels unrelated full reads as ignored memory

evidence.detail: Any receipt.full>=1 marks every non-used retrieved verified/discovery observation ignored; no attempted path/chunk overlap is required.
That correlation is folded into terminal observation.reused drafts.
Ignored counters are replayed into each observation's usage state.
Usefulness affects candidate ordering before lexical relevance.
Ignored counts subtract from usefulness.
The current test asserts this cohort-wide negative attribution rather than observing a relevant reread.

trigger: A turn is served memory for chunk A and performs a legitimate full read for an unrelated missing target B, without a skip/narrow for A.
consequence: A is recorded as reread-despite even though it was not reread. Coupled with compilation clipping, unshown items can receive the same negative label. Counters do change ranking, but they are not reliable measures of model use or task improvement.
suggestedFix: Correlate only emitted records against actual attempted/covered source identities; distinguish unrelated reads, necessary freshness refresh, shown-but-unobserved and explicit rejection. Preserve unknown instead of manufacturing negative evidence.
acceptanceProbe: Serve A, perform a full read of B and assert no ignored signal for A. Then explicitly reread A despite a current reusable excerpt and assert the intended signal. Add clipping and freshness-refresh cases; validate held-out task success separately from read savings.
observed: A bounded fixture with one known chunk and one full-read receipt carrying no covered identity produced an ignored/reread-despite signal.

title: Playbook scope is accepted and stored but does not constrain runtime application

evidence.detail: The public scope schema accepts repository, glob and agent-type restrictions.
Authoring accepts that scope as a validated proposal field.
Runtime loading filters only the bound workspace, status and expiry, not scope restrictions.
All valid active rules are vouched as operator instructions without evaluating applicability.
The gate checks status, expiry, enforcement and trigger, but never scope.
The actual consumer supplies no current paths/agent identity to resolve glob or agent scope.

trigger: An operator authors a rule limited to another repository, Rust paths or a particular agent type, then runs its matching tool trigger outside that declared scope in the same bound workspace.
consequence: The rule is still injected and can warn/block outside its intended applicability. This undermines reusable language-specific procedures and the public promise of scope-limited playbooks. No OS sandbox escape is claimed.
suggestedFix: Apply a canonical scope evaluator before both prompt selection and deterministic gating, supplying current project/agent/path context. If a restriction cannot yet be evaluated, reject or visibly declare it unsupported instead of silently accepting it.
acceptanceProbe: For the same trigger, vary repository, glob and current agent independently. Out-of-scope calls receive no instruction/verdict; an in-scope call retains its existing warn/block behavior. Unsupported applicability is explicit and survives serialization.
observed: The gate produced a verdict for a schema-shaped rule restricted to another public fixture project, Rust globs and a Rust specialist.

title: Degraded V2 authority silently reinjects V1 despite reporting no fallback

evidence.detail: The public configuration contract says unavailable opt-in V2 injects nothing rather than falling back to V1.
Degradation clears memoryV2Context but preserves active=sqlite-v2-opt-in and fallbackOccurred=false.
The authoritative-context helper returns undefined when cleared V2 context fails parsing.
The V1 compiler gate is taskMemory && !getCorrelatedAuthoritativeV2(state), so degraded opt-in state receives a V1 message.
Provider-open failure under opt-in is intentionally passed to the SDK as a V2 config without a repository.

trigger: V2 storage open, migration, lifecycle append or query fails while a valid V1 compatibility task-memory record is available.
consequence: Provider-facing request construction emits V1 memory, while authority state and documented degraded semantics still say V2 is active and no fallback occurred. Human/client consumers cannot accurately know the source used.
suggestedFix: Choose and document one degradation policy, then make request construction and authority telemetry agree: either suppress V1 under opt-in failure or perform an explicit supported fallback with active source/fallback fields updated. Keep active operational memory policy deliberate.
acceptanceProbe: At the real request-construction seam, prepare opt-in V2 with no repository and populated V1 memory; inspect captured messages and authority event. Repeat query throw/invalid result/lifecycle failure, with V1 present/absent. Reported authority must match the injected source.
coverageLimit: The Boolean branch is directly visible; no provider-facing run was invoked to probe this additional issue.

title: Main checkpoint continuation replaces the journal identity before completed-tool replay

evidence.detail: Matching checkpoint restores mainAgentState and sets resumeInterruptedTurn=true.
Only pinnedRunId skips startAgentRun; normal checkpoint continuation mints and assigns a new runId at 1973.
Production startAgentRun returns a fresh local-run UUID.
Completed-result lookup uses the now-current agentState.runId.
Wiring test manually supplies the old runId to the reader instead of executing checkpoint continuation.

trigger: A process dies after a programmatic tool_result was committed but before the next checkpoint; the TUI reloads the older checkpoint and resends its matching prompt.
consequence: Observed DI: replay lookup runs under a new ID while the original completed result remains present. Inference: re-derived non-idempotent programmatic calls can execute again because the old result is unreachable to this guard.
suggestedFix: Pin the interrupted main run's durable identity, with an explicit fresh-turn versus resume contract; preserve/reconstruct replay position against that journal rather than reminting it.
acceptanceProbe: Seed an original journal and older main checkpoint; resume through the real SDK/loop with a unique production-style startAgentRun; assert the completed effect's counter stays one, the old stream remains authoritative, and a subsequent new user turn gets a fresh identity.

title: Model-driven tool dispatch lacks P2 journal boundaries and uncertain-effect reconciliation

evidence.detail: Model-native calls enter executeToolCall directly; custom/MCP calls use executeCustomToolCall at 731.
tool_call/tool_result journal boundaries and completed-result replay live in executeSingleToolCall's programmatic path.
Shared executor only force-flushes an optional writer; it does not append tool boundary events.
Production SDK dispatch calls handleToolCall without P2 journal writer/reader; its signature at 2180–2265 has none.
Optional Memory V2 observation runs after handled output; it is not the P2 replay contract.
MCP dispatch calls the external tool and returns output directly.
No completed match means live re-execution; no ambiguous-effect receipt is returned.
The kill-9-labelled fixture appends B's intent without executing B pre-crash.

trigger: A model-selected shell/custom/MCP operation applies, then the process dies before the next recoverable transcript/result; or a programmatic effect applies between its intent and result records.
consequence: Observed DI: model read_files runs and enters history while the P2 journal has only llm_request/llm_response/step_boundary. Static production trace confirms no SDK compensation for these missing boundaries. Inference: restart cannot distinguish 'not applied' from 'applied but unacknowledged' and may repeat non-idempotent effects.
suggestedFix: Put effect intent/result recording at a shared native/custom/MCP dispatch boundary. Persist a stable operation identity and classify uncertain results explicitly; reconcile supported external effects or require a concrete user decision before repeating them. Keep filesystem broker recovery separate and reuse its receipts where applicable.
acceptanceProbe: Use a DI counter and a real temporary journal; kill a helper after the counter increments but before its result receipt. Restart the actual dispatcher and assert no blind repeat: it must reconcile, report an unknown outcome, or request the required decision. Include native model tools, programmatic tools, custom tools and MCP.
scope: P2 run-journal/replay coverage. This finding does not claim filesystem broker receipts, process-job records, or optional Memory V2 traces are absent.

title: Parent turn cleanup closes the shared journal while detached children are still running

evidence.detail: The TUI closes the journal at the parent run promise-chain end.
Headless command also closes the journal when its parent run returns.
Detached child receives the same journal writer/reader references.
Own-journal re-drive is deliberately launched detached with inherited params.
After close, append silently returns.
Close contract explicitly acknowledges that an outliving child stops journaling.

trigger: A background agent, including a resumed child, outlives the successful/cancelled parent turn whose CLI opened its journal.
consequence: Its later requests, results, and terminal tail are dropped. Inference: a later process restart may reconstruct stale child history, leave a respawn marker unsettled, or lose the result; avoiding closed-database exceptions does not preserve child durability.
suggestedFix: Give journals session/process ownership with child-aware reference counting, or give each detached child an independently owned connection. Persist settlement to the current durable parent/session record rather than only mutating a captured old AgentState.
acceptanceProbe: Hold a child on a DI gate, let the parent return and perform real CLI cleanup, release the child, reopen the disk journal, and assert the child's final result/tail and parent settlement exist. Repeat with cooperative parent cancellation.

title: ACP prompts and session/load do not restore an executable conversation

evidence.detail: Each prompt calls client.run without previousRun, onCheckpoint or P2 journal handles; returned RunState is discarded.
SDK conversation continuation requires passing previousRun.
Durable ACP store contains receipt, gate, capability and workspace-revision maps, not the transcript/main AgentState.
Chat-history replay requires optional historyLoader, which runServe does not wire.
Derived loader ignores restoreFromJournal=false.
Resume/replay advertisement derives from journalAvailable.
hasJournal checks only whether journalDir was configured.

trigger: Send a follow-up in one ACP session, or load its ID after a serve restart, including an ID with no journal.
consequence: Observed DI: the second prompt carries no prior RunState; an absent session loads successfully with {} while journal availability is advertised. The model's prior conversation and executable workflow state do not continue even though receipt/gate projections can reload.
suggestedFix: Create a per-session durable RunState/transcript owner; route previousRun and checkpoint/journal handles through it and provide the actual history loader. Advertise executable resume only when this path is available, and return typed missing/corrupt-session outcomes.
acceptanceProbe: Run two DI prompts where the second depends on a first-turn constraint, then restart the service over a temp store and load the ID. Assert the core sees that constraint, history is replayed, checkpoints use the same session, and invented/missing IDs fail distinctly.

title: ACP reattachment loses running-turn cancellation ownership and bypasses the prompt guard

evidence.detail: Every socket creates a fresh ACP agent with its own private session map.
Run AbortControllers are stored in that per-connection map.
Loading on a fresh connection creates a record with a null controller; it only preserves an existing same-connection controller.
The concurrent-prompt guard checks that connection-local controller.
Detach destroys the owned transport and keeps the session ID for load on a new connection.
Cancel addresses only the current connection's session record.
Socket detach test waits until the prompt completed; it does not exercise a live reattachment.

trigger: Detach/reconnect or connect another authorized client and load an ID while the original long tool/model turn remains live.
consequence: Observed DI with two production-style agents sharing one store: cancellation on the loaded session does not abort the original run, and a second prompt is admitted before the first settles. Inference: two runs can mutate the same served workspace with no session-level guard or usable control over the first.
suggestedFix: Own running turns in a service-wide session registry and attach connection sinks/controllers to that owner. Define detach and disconnect semantics explicitly; a new client must observe/join/cancel the same turn and preserve the per-session prompt exclusion.
acceptanceProbe: Hold a first run on a gate; disconnect and reconnect through the actual socket backend; load its ID and attempt cancel/another prompt. Assert cancel reaches the original controller and a new prompt is rejected until settlement or explicitly queued.
assuranceLimit: The DI probe uses two connection-level agents; no real socket disconnect was executed. Installed ACP 1.5 legacy adapter passes params to implementation.prompt without its connection request signal; vendor code is excluded from the structural receipt.

title: A killed socket service leaves an anonymous lock that blocks restart indefinitely

evidence.detail: Socket lock is exclusively created but receives no PID/token/owner record.
Any existing lock is refused before stale-socket cleanup.
Lock removal is only graceful cleanup or bind/setup error handling.
Cleanup coverage closes gracefully; it does not kill a lock owner.

trigger: The serve process is SIGKILLed or crashes after acquiring socketPath.lock; the user restarts serve at the same socket path.
consequence: Observed DI: the production startup path refuses an otherwise safe directory containing that anonymous stale lock. An actual process kill cannot execute releaseLock, so automatic restart remains blocked until manual cleanup.
suggestedFix: Use a crash-recoverable, ownership-verified lock with a recorded owner and safe stale-owner reconciliation, reusing proven store lock patterns. Surface recoverable stale-lock versus live-owner conflict distinctly.
acceptanceProbe: Launch a temp socket service, wait for ownership, SIGKILL the helper, restart at the identical path and verify successful bind without deleting another live owner's lock. Also cover stale socket/non-socket refusal and permission failure.

title: Live child path leases expire because production spawns never heartbeat them

evidence.detail: Default lease TTL is thirty minutes.
The next acquisition sweeps expired runtime leases without checking child liveness.
Real batch spawn acquires a lease and only releases it in settle/rollback paths.
Inline spawn uses the same acquire/release pattern.
Extension helper exists; repository consumer search found only tests calling it.
Productive subagent durations are unbounded by default.

trigger: A writable child runs past the thirty-minute TTL and another child requests an overlapping path.
consequence: Observed shortened-TTL DI: overlap is admitted while the original durable lease still says active. The advertised exclusive child scope ceases to exclude a still-running writer. Separate processes also have independent path maps; the exported disk-backed WorkspaceLeaseService is not wired into spawns.
suggestedFix: Tie lease renewal/release to actual child supervision and cancellation; route participating processes through one durable lease authority if cross-process ownership is promised. Preserve fencing/generation checks so an expired owner cannot resume writing after a replacement acquires.
acceptanceProbe: With an injected clock, keep one writable child live across multiple TTLs, request overlap, and assert refusal until terminal settlement. Exercise abrupt owner death, lost renewal, cancellation and a stale owner's attempted renewal.

title: Shipped base2 requests a workflow helper that the runtime does not inject

evidence.detail: Control-plane generator params expose transitionBase2Gate.
Shipped consumer exclusively reads transitionBase2GateSafe.
A typeof function guard skips all workflowStates updates when that member is absent.
Tests exercise the safe helper in isolation, not its injected production name.

trigger: A normal base2 gate telemetry event tries to advance its persisted advisory workflow.
consequence: No advisory state/revision update or structured illegal-transition result is recorded through this branch. This is an unwired telemetry/resumability feature; it does not establish a defect in the authoritative generator gate (owned by pair03).
suggestedFix: Expose the safe helper under the member name the serialized consumer expects and give the injected control-plane contract one typed/shared definition.
acceptanceProbe: Drive the real runProgrammaticStep-to-shipped-base2 path without manually adding the helper; assert workflowStates revision advances and an illegal transition persists a structured error while authoritative gate behavior remains unchanged.

title: Concurrent snapshot producers can orphan a snapshot they report as created

evidence.detail: Successful-turn snapshot runs fire-and-forget before the queue is released.
Each producer separately reads the private ref's current parent.
Publication uses unconditional update-ref without an expected old SHA.
Guard excludes bisection but does not serialize concurrent snapshot producers.
Concurrency coverage concerns bisection ownership, not two snapshot publications.

trigger: Two CLI processes, or a slow prior-turn snapshot and another producer, capture distinct trees and read the same private-ref tip before publishing.
consequence: Observed DI: both return created but publish sibling commits with the same parent through unconditional update-ref. Inference: only the last remains in the listed chain; one successful recovery point can disappear, and a slow end-turn capture can contain later mutations.
suggestedFix: Serialize capture and publication per repository and compare-and-swap the expected ref tip. Define a bounded turn/shell snapshot barrier; cancel or mark late captures accurately instead of letting them publish a later tree as an earlier boundary.
acceptanceProbe: Use two temp-repo producers with barriers at parent read/publication; assert both successful snapshots remain in one chain or one fails/retries explicitly. Queue a fast mutating next turn behind a slow capture and verify turn attribution.

title: JSON replay emits empty assistant text for the runtime's response record shape

evidence.detail: Runtime llm_response stores {messageId, fullResponse}.
JSON mapper reads only payload.text or payload.message, falling back to empty text.
The mapper is the actual --json replay/export consumer.

trigger: Run openbuff replay <id> --json against an ordinary journalled plain assistant response produced by the runtime.
consequence: Observed DI with the production payload shape: replay exits zero and emits {type:'text',text:''}; the retained assistant answer disappears from the machine-readable replay/evaluation fixture.
suggestedFix: Define and share a versioned journal response schema that explicitly stores model-visible text; make replay consume it and handle existing fullResponse rows deliberately without re-executing tools.
acceptanceProbe: Journal a plain response through the real loop, replay --json, and assert the original visible text and ordering survive. Include legacy rows, tool-containing responses and empty/error records.

title: Stale-lock recovery can remove a fresh live broker lock and admit two successful CAS writers

evidence.detail: After asynchronous canRecoverLock, the stale breaker recursively removes the current lock path without a generation-safe takeover.
Exact-byte beforeHash equality is trusted under that workspace lock before staging and replacement.
The stale-lock test checks dead versus live owners sequentially, not competing breakers and lock reacquisition.

trigger: B decides an old lock is stale; A removes the old generation and acquires a fresh live lock before B reaches fs.rm.
consequence: A and B both return applied=true for the same expected original hash, and A overwrites the bytes B successfully committed. The bounded public-API probe observed B revision 2 completing before A revision 1.
suggestedFix: Serialize stale recovery with a recovery claim honored by all acquisitions and perform generation-safe takeover; never remove the current lock from a prior asynchronous stale decision. Use an OS-backed lock if portable primitives cannot supply the necessary invariant.
acceptanceProbe: Run two writers/breakers with deterministic pauses at stale decision and staging. Exactly one commit against a shared original hash may succeed; a fresh live lock must remain owned and no receipt may claim an overwritten successful CAS.
inference: The probe used two broker instances in one process and internal DI to widen existing awaits. Shared filesystem locking makes the same interleaving applicable across processes; its spontaneous frequency was not measured.

title: Semantic edits discard document versions and the splice preimage before conditional commit

evidence.detail: WorkspaceEdit normalization intentionally ignores textDocument.version.
rename returns only the flattened changesByUri map.
The service reads disk text and returns only path/newContent for the splice.
The apply core forwards unguarded full-file contents without expectedHash; its comment incorrectly claims the later snapshot protects the service-read interval.
The coordinator derives a new beforeContent snapshot after the service splice.

trigger: A file changes after the language-service splice but before changeFiles prepares, or a server WorkspaceEdit names a document version that differs from the open document.
consequence: The later CAS protects the newly read file while committing content derived from older bytes. The external append in the fixture disappeared and applied=true was returned. A protocol fixture with didOpen version 1 and WorkspaceEdit version 999 also applied without a stale-version error.
suggestedFix: Retain a versioned per-document exact preimage through WorkspaceEdit normalization, service splicing and the apply core; bind the coordinator to that exact hash rather than a newly adopted snapshot.
acceptanceProbe: Pause between service read and apply; append external text or change only EOL/BOM bytes. Reject without writes and preserve the external bytes. Reject a mismatched documentChanges version before any splice or mutation.

title: A rejected commit followed by rollback conflict is promoted to a confirmed applied action

evidence.detail: The in-progress action enters committed before the adapter result is known.
Failure receipts snapshot whatever bytes exist now, including an external writer's state.
Every rollback_failed receipt action becomes outcome=applied, regardless of whether the forward commit applied.
The confirmed-action selector accepts applied actions from rollback_incomplete results.
The selected actions drive workspace journal, LSP sync and mutation observers.

trigger: An external writer wins immediately before the forward conditionalCommit, and rollback rejects because the target is not the transaction's proposed after-content.
consequence: Both adapter calls returned applied=false in the probe, but the resulting action and getConfirmedAppliedActionsV1 reported applied. The SDK can attribute unrelated external bytes to an agent mutation and advance its evidence using false positive authority.
suggestedFix: Record forward-commit evidence separately from rollback attempts. Unknown or externally diverged rollback state must not become confirmed applied; carry observed hashes as uncertain state requiring invalidation rather than success proof.
acceptanceProbe: Inject an external write before CAS and reject both forward and rollback calls. Preserve the external bytes, return zero confirmed applied actions, and ensure SDK/runtime observers cannot publish the intended edit as committed.

title: Startup transaction recovery overwrites divergent bytes without establishing transaction ownership

evidence.detail: Intent entries retain beforeHash/beforeBytes but no expected after-state.
Divergence is merely current text != preimage text.
A mixed transaction reverts every divergent path.
The production restoration callback uses unconditional unlink/writeFile.
Actual run initialization invokes this recovery callback with the run filesystem.

trigger: An interrupted multi-file intent has at least one untouched path and one path whose current bytes belong to an external writer rather than the transaction.
consequence: The fixture external content was replaced by the old preimage and recovery returned ok=true. A read failure also falls back to unconditional restoration, so insufficient evidence weakens rather than strengthens the ownership check.
suggestedFix: Persist planned after-hashes/action receipts and recover only bytes proven transaction-owned through conditional primitives. Preserve unknown or external state as unresolved; divergence from a preimage is not a commit/ownership proof.
acceptanceProbe: Crash/fault after one action, then externally change that path and leave another path at its preimage. Recovery must preserve external bytes and report unresolved state. Repeat for created files, moves, read failures and all-diverged but unrecognized states.
inference: No OS process was killed in this audit; durable tx_begin plus controlled fixture state reproduced the production startup restoration logic.

title: Failed startup rollback is terminally aborted and excluded from later recovery

evidence.detail: A tx_abort marker is appended even when a restoration threw.
Only transactions whose last event is tx_begin are eligible for another recovery.
The once-per-process key is set before attempting recovery; structured recovery failure is not inspected.

trigger: Restoring an interrupted transaction fails transiently, such as a write permission or I/O error.
consequence: The injected restore failure returned ok=false with unchanged divergent bytes, yet a subsequent recoverInterruptedTransactions returned an empty list because tx_abort had resolved it. The normal SDK startup also suppresses another in-process attempt.
suggestedFix: Persist recovery_required/rollback_incomplete as nonterminal, keep unfinished path ownership evidence, and set the recovery-performed key only on a conclusive successful result. Surface unresolved workspace state to mutation callers.
acceptanceProbe: Fail one recovery write, then restore filesystem availability. A later recovery must retry and finish the remaining paths; a process restart must still see the unresolved intent. Do not silently proceed as if recovery completed.

title: Incomplete semantic WorkspaceEdits commit a subset and can report full apply

evidence.detail: Unsupported resource operations are recorded as skipped during normalization.
rename drops skipped diagnostics and resource-operation metadata.
Successful per-file splices are retained even if peers fail.
applied mirrors the subset coordinator outcome; service failures do not make it false.
The UI may display partial when an error survived, but cannot undo a broken semantic operation.

trigger: One consumer edit has an invalid/overlapping/unreadable range, or a rename WorkspaceEdit includes an unsupported RenameFile/DeleteFile/resource operation alongside usable text edits.
consequence: The declaration fixture changed foo to bar while its consumer retained foo, and the tool returned applied=true plus an error. In a real multiplexer protocol fixture, the requested file rename was omitted entirely and text edits applied with no error.
suggestedFix: Preserve every normalized operation and refusal reason. For rename/refactor, reject the entire edit before mutation when any required member cannot apply; translate supported lifecycle operations into the canonical coordinator. Explicitly label any intentionally supported partial mode.
acceptanceProbe: Rename a declaration and consumers with one failed member and with a resource rename. Either apply the complete WorkspaceEdit or leave all files untouched with structured unavailable/error details; applied=true must mean the requested operation completed.

title: UTF-8 BOM stripping breaks exact preimages and causes permanently stale edits

evidence.detail: Default UTF-8 TextDecoder strips the BOM.
Transaction preimages use the same BOM-stripping decoder.
The conditional expected hash is reconstructed from decoded beforeContent.
The default broker compares the hash of original raw bytes.

trigger: A supported UTF-8 source file begins with EF BB BF and is read, then edited through the normal transaction coordinator.
consequence: The read returns ok with authority over BOM-stripped text. The coordinator's reconstructed preimage hash does not match the raw file, so commit is refused indefinitely even after rereading. The untouched fixture was reported rollback_incomplete; the false applied action is separately covered by F3.
suggestedFix: Retain original bytes/BOM metadata as the authoritative preimage and decode losslessly for text edits. Keep normalized content freshness separate from the raw hash used for CAS, receipts and recovery.
acceptanceProbe: Read and edit a BOM+CRLF file through the default SDK path, including create/edit/delete/move and rollback. Preserve BOM, untouched bytes, mode and final-newline state, and issue matching exact receipts without a stale loop.

title: Scoped range and symbol transaction edits normalize unrelated CRLF bytes to LF

evidence.detail: replace_range constructs output from the whole LF-normalized snapshot.
rewrite_symbol also splits normalized whole-file text and joins with LF.
The real runtime forwards the prepared EOL-changing patch through the canonical SDK coordinator.
The separate str_replace implementation restores original per-line endings.
Mixed EOL preservation tests exercise str_replace, not all canonical edit variants.

trigger: A capability authorizes one line or symbol of a CRLF/mixed-EOL source and edit_transaction applies replace_range/rewrite_symbol.
consequence: A real broker-backed one-line range edit changed all three CRLF terminators to LF while returning applied. Bytes outside the authorized text span changed; existing str_replace preservation does not cover the other variants.
suggestedFix: Share a lossless splice/EOL preservation implementation across every localized transaction variant; use normalized text only for matching and coordinates, not as the whole-file output base.
acceptanceProbe: Exercise every localized variant on CRLF, mixed LF/CRLF, BOM, astral Unicode and no-final-newline fixtures. Assert byte equality outside the selected span after commit and after rollback.
inference: rewrite_symbol shares the directly inspected normalization but only replace_range was executed in the bounded probe.

title: Server edit ranges accept negative, fractional and reversed coordinates

evidence.detail: Normalization checks only typeof number, not safe integer/nonnegative/ordered bounds.
Offset validation has an upper bound but no character lower bound or integer check.
The splice assumes startOffset <= endOffset and JavaScript slice coerces fractional offsets.

trigger: A malformed language-server WorkspaceEdit contains negative/fractional characters or an end before its start; CRLF boundary disagreement is also accepted up to the carriage return.
consequence: Negative coordinates on line 2 edited bytes in line 1. A reversed range duplicated text; fractional coordinates were silently truncated. The full multiplexer/service/apply probe confirmed negative server positions can reach disk with applied=true.
suggestedFix: Validate finite safe integer coordinates, nonnegative characters/lines, start <= end, line-content bounds excluding CRLF, and a supported negotiated position encoding before splicing.
acceptanceProbe: Reject negative, fractional, nonfinite, reversed, overshooting and CRLF-terminator ranges without writes. Test valid UTF-16 astral positions and explicitly reject/convert unsupported UTF-8/UTF-32 encodings.
inference: Valid default LSP UTF-16 coordinates match JavaScript string units. No compliant-server UTF-8/UTF-32 negotiation or cross-language live position task was exercised.

title: Supported multi-file preimages exceed the intent log cap and silently lose crash recovery

evidence.detail: A transaction permits 16 MiB/file and 64 MiB rollback state.
The default complete intent log cap is 8 MiB, including serialized preimages.
Failed tx_begin logs a warning and proceeds with mutation without a durable preimage.
The current test explicitly expects commit success after an intent-log failure.

trigger: A valid multi-file transaction has a serialized preimage larger than the default 8 MiB log cap, or logging cannot persist the intent.
consequence: The 9 MiB+small-file fixture committed both files, returned applied, and emitted neither an intent log nor a transactionId. Durability is reduced to in-memory rollback without an explicit tool result degradation.
suggestedFix: Align mutation admission with durable preimage capacity and fail before the first commit when required durability cannot be recorded. Any optional nondurable mode should be explicit in the public result and caller policy.
acceptanceProbe: Submit 8/9 MiB aggregate preimages and escaping-heavy text under default limits. If the durable intent cannot fit or fsync fails, assert no file changes; otherwise kill/fault between commits and recover the complete group.
inference: Crash midway after the observed missing intent would have no group preimage to recover; this consequence follows statically and was not measured by killing a process.

title: Bounded text ranges allocate an entire unbroken line even when maxBytes is tiny

evidence.detail: Every scanned line accumulates currentParts irrespective of requested range or truncation.
The full line is concatenated before finishLine checks the return budget.
The final unterminated line is also concatenated without a bound.
Oversized reads delegate to this bounded-text capability.

trigger: An oversized file contains a large single line before, inside or after the requested range.
consequence: A 24 MiB fixture with maxBytes=1024 returned zero bytes but performed a 24 MiB Buffer.concat. The return payload is bounded; reader working memory grows with the longest scanned line and can undermine observation availability.
suggestedFix: Count newlines without retaining irrelevant or over-budget lines; cap the pending selected line to the allowed budget and discard the rest while continuing bounded metadata counting. Add cancellable read capability support where needed.
acceptanceProbe: Read a very long selected/unselected line with a 1 KiB budget and instrument peak buffered/concatenated bytes. Bound memory by request budget plus fixed chunk overhead; maintain correct complete/totalLines metadata and close the stream on cancellation.
inference: The probe instrumented Buffer.concat in a disposable process; it is not an RSS, latency or throughput benchmark. Larger-file exhaustion risk follows from the unbounded allocation.

title: Broker receipt recovery can follow a replaced parent symlink outside the workspace

evidence.detail: Recovery absoluteFromRelative checks lexical containment only.
Recovered delete reads and unlinks the persisted staging path without checking its current canonical parent.
Ordinary mutation resolvePath does check the canonical parent, unlike recovery.
Default broker construction performs this pending-receipt recovery at real run startup.

trigger: A legitimate pending receipt survives a partial mutation; its original directory is moved outside the workspace and the former parent is replaced with a symlink to that directory.
consequence: Fresh broker startup unlinked a tombstone outside its own root and finalized recovered_committed in the fixture. No receipt tampering was needed. Recovery has a weaker path authority than normal commits.
suggestedFix: Reauthorize every recovered source, destination and staging path against current canonical containment and ownership; preserve unresolved receipts when path identity changed. Use anchored handles/native path primitives when the boundary requires exclusion of external races.
acceptanceProbe: For pending commit/delete/move receipts, replace a parent directory with a symlink to an outside fixture before recovery. Do not read, unlink or replace outside bytes; retain a recovery_required receipt with an actionable error.

title: Current packaging omits tag queries and relies on checkout-dependent asset lookup

evidence.detail: Tag queries are bare filenames, no longer bundled .scm imports.
Queries load through filesystem candidates including the module and executable directory.
Dynamic dirname falls back to require.resolve(@codebuff/code-map), which current Bun bundles resolve to the build checkout.

Every successful new index has builtAt=Date.now(), including a precise refresh.
Safety scheduling tests isIndexStale(this.index), which is based only on that most recent builtAt.
Subtrees beyond the Linux watcher cap depend on the age-based integrity sweep.

trigger: An external edit is missed by a capped/failed watcher while the agent continues confirmed precise mutations more frequently than the five-minute stale age.
consequence: Each unrelated precise refresh makes index age zero, so the missed external edit can remain invisible for an unbounded busy session. Watcher fallback is eventual only if enough idle age occurs, not under continuous edits.
