suggestedFix: Track last successful full reconciliation separately from the latest snapshot build time, and schedule that sweep on its own monotonic deadline even while precise deltas continue. Preserve queued deltas and distinguish full-sweep coverage from incremental liveness.
acceptanceProbe: With a fake clock and precise deltas every four minutes, an unobserved sibling edit must converge within the declared full-sweep interval without an idle period; repeat after watcher degradation and at the descriptor cap.

title: Whitespace normalization erases executable newlines and exact approval identity

evidence.detail: normalizeCommand collapses all whitespace, including quoted text and newlines.
hashCommand hashes the collapsed string while claiming exact command binding.
Classification normalizes before the newline-aware scanner.
Only a nonempty classification enters high-impact authorization.
Full-log basher execution itself constructs a multiline shell wrapper.

trigger: Use a newline-separated assistant command such as printf safe followed by a Python -c one-liner; alternatively change internal whitespace in an approved quoted payload.
consequence: A real full-access terminal probe executed both harmless statements with zero authorization calls. Two distinct quoted Node payloads produced identical action, target, and command hash, so the receipt comparison cannot distinguish their bytes.
suggestedFix: Hash the exact executable bytes; parse the original command without flattening shell separators or quoted operands. Keep any display normalization separate from authority.
acceptanceProbe: A newline-separated high-impact second command reaches authorization in balanced and strict modes; approvals for quoted payloads differing by a space or newline are rejected as mismatches.

title: The first classified effect masks later high-impact effects in a compound command

evidence.detail: Compound classification returns immediately on the first recognized segment.
Balanced mode only examines the single action handed to it.
Production authorization evaluates that single classification.

trigger: Put a routine recognized action before a risky effect, for example npm install fixture && rm -rf fixture, or git push origin feature && terraform apply.
consequence: Pure production-function probes classified only dependency-install or push and returned allowed with approvalRequired:false; later deletion/deployment is never evaluated. The defect also applies inside recursively inspected shell payloads.

acceptanceProbe: Vary the ordering of routine, destructive, remote, and deployment segments: every risky effect requires the expected decision, and no earlier routine command suppresses it.

title: Balanced mode allows force and delete pushes to feature branches

evidence.detail: Push parsing retains only action push, branch and target; destructive flags are not risk attributes.
The balanced high-impact set excludes push.
Push approval is conditional only on a known default-branch match.
Product policy explicitly retains force/delete/default-branch push gating.

acceptanceProbe: Probe -f, --force-with-lease, --delete, plus-prefixed and deletion refspecs, default-branch destinations, and ambiguous upstream pushes in all three modes.

title: Canonical provider credentials are stripped for terminal commands but inherited by adjacent launchers

evidence.detail: Raw system environment must not be handed to child processes.
Compiler runner inherits by omission or merges raw host environment with overrides.
LSP spawns with cwd alone, implicitly inheriting the host environment.
Chrome pipe launcher omits an explicit child environment.
Tool version probes inherit the host environment.

trigger: The host has a canonical BYOK key and runs a diagnostic/compiler, language server, browser, or discovery/index subprocess.

title: Shell leader exit cancels escalation while descendants remain alive

evidence.detail: Timeout/abort begins group TERM with a five-second KILL timer.
Shell close settles the operation and clears the escalation timer.
Any background settlement clears its pending escalation.
Leader exit settles the background job stopped.
A settled job refuses subsequent kill attempts.

trigger: A command creates a TERM-ignoring child with redirected output, then waits; cancellation or a finite timeout kills the shell leader first.
consequence: After 5.5 seconds the SYNC result was timedOut while its child remained sleeping. BACKGROUND reported stopped while its child remained sleeping, and a later SIGKILL request returned killed:false. These were ordinary process-group descendants, not escaped sessions.
suggestedFix: Keep process-scope termination supervision independent of leader close and registry settlement; confirm the owned scope is empty before claiming completion, or report an explicit uncertain/live-descendant state.
acceptanceProbe: For timeout, abort, and kill use redirected-output children that ignore TERM; verify group KILL still happens after leader exit and no child remains after the grace period. Add platform-specific guarantees without changing unbounded defaults.

title: Output-quota failure makes a live background process unkillable through its job

evidence.detail: Quota breach settles the job as terminal error before signaling.
Quota path sends TERM without scheduling KILL escalation.
killBackgroundJob refuses every state except running.

trigger: A background process exceeds the 10 MiB log quota and ignores TERM.
consequence: The probe log was bounded at 10,485,760 bytes, but after 5.5 seconds its process was still sleeping. A SIGKILL request through the job returned killed:false because status was already error.
suggestedFix: Record quota failure separately from process liveness, retain kill authority while the process is alive, and run bounded TERM/KILL cleanup before dropping the handle.
acceptanceProbe: A TERM-ignoring output flood becomes an error with bounded logs and confirmed dead process scope; a user kill remains effective while quota cleanup is pending.

trigger: A summary retains the right source path but drops or contradicts the planted backoff value, requirement, blocker state or outcome.
consequence: The advertised aggregate can remain perfect despite semantic information loss. The fixture probe replaced 1500ms with 0ms while keeping the path and received expected=1, missing=[]; citing read:path with all history dropped also returned complete coverage. This does not prove the underlying memory runtime fails, only that this oracle cannot establish value fidelity.
suggestedFix: Name identifier coverage accurately and add independent planted-value/constraint/negation/blocker-state oracles. Drive actual compaction/consolidation seams with faithful and adversarial injected summaries across archive aging and restart; keep useful archive/path tests.
acceptanceProbe: Require the right path with a wrong value, omitted negation, resolved-versus-open blocker inversion and aged archive to lower the value-fidelity score. A faithful summary must preserve both identity and factual content over several passes.

title: Benchmark task execution shares the controller key environment and home

evidence.detail: Repository setup shell receives the complete process.env plus task overrides.
Final checks likewise inherit the complete controller process environment.
Restricted install env still uses the real controller HOME.
npm/bun package lifecycle code runs directly on the host in a temporary cwd.
Nightly workflow exports named repository secrets to subsequent evaluator steps.

trigger: A third-party benchmark setup/check/package lifecycle script runs while provider or other service keys remain available to the controller.
consequence: A temporary repository cwd is not OS isolation or a separate key lifecycle. An artificial controller token was readable by a check and written into the owned fixture file. No real credentials, home configuration or exfiltration endpoint were read or used. Normal intentional full-access coding-body behavior is not being classified as an authorization defect.
suggestedFix: For untrusted evaluation code, isolate repo/check/install execution with a key-free environment and ephemeral home, leaving provider access in the controller through a defined channel. Alternatively require an explicit trusted-task execution mode and record that weaker assurance. Do not silently change the body runtime full-access contract.
acceptanceProbe: Use dummy environment and home-file canaries only: third-party setup/check/install code must not see controller canaries under the isolated mode, while fake provider calls still work and the receipt states the actual isolation boundary.

title: Runner debug errors bypass artifact path sanitization

evidence.detail: Error-event debug filename interpolates raw commitId and agentId.
Output-error debug filename repeats raw identifiers under a fixed source directory.
Task id/sha validation imposes no path/hex restriction.
The normal trace path separately sanitizes identifiers, which does not protect the earlier runner write.

trigger: An eval task or supplied runner agent identifier contains traversal components, and an SDK error occurs.
consequence: The debug artifact can escape the intended evaluator/log root and fail or write into another directory. The error-output fixture used a relative traversal ID and the real runner created its debug file in this shard's explicitly owned /tmp fixture directory. Random suffixes limit exact-file overwrite targeting but do not provide containment.
suggestedFix: Route all debug artifacts through the run-owned artifact writer; sanitize filenames and enforce resolved containment. Keep raw identifiers as data fields inside the artifact.
acceptanceProbe: Inject ../ and absolute-looking IDs on both event-error and output-error paths; every artifact must stay within an injected run directory, with no writes to source/home or unrelated fixture paths.

title: Minute-resolution log directories mix independent run evidence

evidence.detail: Log key truncates the timestamp to YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM and adds only sanitized agent names.
An existing same-key directory is reused.
Meta-analysis scans every ANALYSIS filename found in that directory.
FINAL_RESULTS.json overwrites the same filename.

trigger: Two evaluator invocations with the same agent list begin in the same minute, including retries or parallel variants.
consequence: Task traces/FINAL_RESULTS can overwrite, stale ANALYSIS rows can enter the new meta-analysis, and the final file listing can attribute another invocation's artifacts to this run. No existing log directory was opened or live run executed to demonstrate this deterministic naming collision.
suggestedFix: Allocate a unique run ID and create the directory exclusively; write atomic artifact manifests bound to that run and input digests, and have analyzers consume manifest entries instead of a directory-wide name scan.
acceptanceProbe: With a fixed clock, launch two fake-client runs using the same agent names but different tasks/configs and assert disjoint directories/manifests, no overwrite, no cross-run analysis rows and explicit failed-write states.
verification: static trace; no private log records accessed

title: The reviewed-provenance update instruction has no passing CI path

evidence.detail: Comment promises an already-approved identity change can arrive in a separate reviewed commit.
Actual policy compares whole provenance file name-status against the PR base or last parent.
Any status other than A fails; there is no reviewed-update exception.
New resolved releases require a refreshed record.
Tests assert strings/presence, not an approved-update versus unreviewed-update scenario.

trigger: A legitimate dependency upgrade adds a reviewed release entry to the existing provenance JSON, even in its own reviewed commit.
consequence: The offline reconciliation demands new evidence, but the CI file-diff gate rejects every modification of that evidence file. The error's prescribed separate reviewed commit still yields M against the PR base. For batched direct pushes, comparing only HEAD~1 also does not cover the entire pushed range. GitHub execution was not observed.
suggestedFix: Define a reviewable update channel or per-release append/identity policy whose approved new entries can pass while unauthorized changes to existing identities fail. Compare the correct event base/range; keep the useful offline reconciliation and state explicitly that it is not upstream attestation.
acceptanceProbe: Exercise initial addition, unchanged record, approved new release entry, unauthorized existing identity rewrite, deletion and multi-commit push fixtures with the actual guard logic. Approved updates pass and existing-record tampering fails for both PR and push event bases.
verification: static workflow and guard trace; actual GitHub execution unknown

title: Probe-only binary smoke accepts known fatal output

evidence.detail: Capture records fatal patterns on probe stdout/stderr.
requireProbe returns success for code=0 and markerHit without checking fatalHit.
Probe-only mode returns before the full TUI negative fatal gate.
Legacy macOS release validation explicitly selects probe-only mode.

trigger: A packaged native probe reports the expected success marker and exits zero while also printing a known fatal/unhandled rejection.
consequence: The legacy/probe-only release gate can accept contradictory startup evidence. The safe shell fixture emitted Unhandled rejection plus both success markers: probe-only exited 0, whereas the same fixture's full smoke exited 1 after detecting the fatal. These are adversarial harness probes, not evidence about a current installed release binary.
suggestedFix: Require absence of captured fatal markers on every successful probe; settle after stdout/stderr drain and preserve timeout/spawn/error distinctions. Keep full-boot positive checks and bounded capture.
acceptanceProbe: Run a fake binary emitting success+fatal, success-only, missing marker, nonzero exit and late/split fatal output. Both probe-only and full modes must reject every fatal case.

title: Feature receipt snapshot identity is discarded before audit coverage evaluation

evidence.detail: Each feature input must carry snapshot_id.
Mapping drops the nested snapshot_id and schema_version; the FeatureCompletenessRecord retains no identity.
Feature acceptance checks verified/status/file membership, without nested snapshot equality.
nestedFeatureSnapshot: foreign-feature-snapshot passes input schema and returns complete:true with current structural receipts.

trigger: Pass feature evidence from a different snapshot alongside structurally current receipts for matching paths.
consequence: The coverage result advertises exact snapshot binding while accepting feature evidence with another identity.
suggestedFix: Validate every nested feature snapshot against the pinned inventory before normalization; retain identity in the typed feature record and report mismatches explicitly.
acceptanceProbe: Public wrapper with matching nested identities remains successful; foreign/missing identities fail with a specific feature-identity diagnostic, including camelCase compatibility inputs.
inference: The probe demonstrates receipt acceptance, not the quality or frequency of an actual model's feature audit.

title: Cached audit inventories bypass stale-source refusal and mix source generations

evidence.detail: Feature inspection reuses a same-root inventory cache entry; stale checking is only performed on cache misses.
Coverage evaluation uses the same cache-only stale check.
Feature search reads current mutable source bytes against the cached file roster.
cachedSourceDrift: changing small inventoried source changes a fresh inventory hash but cached evaluation still returns complete:true under the old hash.

trigger: Inventory a workspace, modify an inventoried implementation below the byte cap, then inspect/evaluate using the original cached snapshot id.
consequence: Current source can be reported under an older snapshot, and a stale coverage result is accepted without the documented refusal.
suggestedFix: Either pin immutable source bytes and read those throughout the audit, or re-attest full non-live contents before feature inspection and synthesis. Preserve live-state exclusions and project-root binding.
acceptanceProbe: Cache the inventory, change a small source file, and require explicit stale refusal; writing only excluded finding/journal artifacts remains accepted. Repeat across a different cwd with identical bytes.
distinctFrom: The probe modifies a small file below every cap; it does not repeat the root's native large-tail/source-exclusion probes.

title: Reviewer gate accepts foreign source fingerprints and records credit under the expected identity

evidence.detail: Wrong-but-well-formed v3 fingerprints are accepted whenever declared file coverage is complete.
The production caller emits fingerprint drift as telemetry and continues gate processing.
Successful receipt gateId uses the parent's expected fingerprint; per-file hashes are sampled at credit time.
Existing regression explicitly requires accepting a wrong-but-well-formed fingerprint.
Public contract says the runtime verifies the fingerprint against the pending working-tree snapshot.
reviewerForeignFingerprint has no attestation issues/blockers and yields LOOKS_GOOD while telemetry records the foreign token.

trigger: A reviewer returns LOOKS_GOOD over the same declared pending paths but with a source fingerprint different from the parent's expected token.
consequence: Syntax and file membership do not establish inspected bytes; a stale assessment may be credited under an expected/current source identity and later reused as reviewed truth.
suggestedFix: Bind review credit to observed file/read basis references or an immutable reviewed snapshot; reject source-content drift. Exclude unrelated metadata from the identity rather than tolerating arbitrary foreign content fingerprints. Preserve reduced-cost reuse only for unchanged reviewed bytes.
acceptanceProbe: Review source generation A, change the same paths to B, submit A's receipt, and require a fresh review with no B credit. An unrelated findings/journal update with unchanged source must not cause review churn.
assurance: local gate-helper probe plus static production credit trace
inference: No live model or full generator finalization was run. The helper accepts foreign tokens and the caller records credit; the rate of obsolete model assessments is unmeasured.

title: Ordinary reviewer receipts can omit all assessment dimensions and implementation requirements

evidence.detail: All five nested dimensions are optional; requirementCoverage is optional at the top level.
Finalization checks only reported incomplete requirements and reported block-prefixed dimensions.
The lightweight tier deliberately excludes contract-bearing changes.
Runtime semantic guard checks only that the verdict is a known label.
Normal receipt acceptance validates the declared schema, which permits omissions.
reviewerOmittedAssessment: contract file is not lightweight-eligible; dimensions:{} and no requirements have no missing top-level schema fields, no runtime verdict issue, no blockers, and LOOKS_GOOD.

trigger: A normal review of a contract-bearing behavioral change returns a matching fingerprint/file roster and LOOKS_GOOD but dimensions:{} and no requirementCoverage.
consequence: The harness cannot distinguish an omitted assessment from a complete clean review; a full-review policy is weakened without explicit lightweight eligibility.
suggestedFix: Use typed dimension outcomes and require every ordinary-review dimension plus coverage of an established user/plan requirement roster. Permit explicit n/a with evidence and preserve the opt-in lightweight escalation mechanism.
acceptanceProbe: A standard contract-file review missing a dimension or known implementation requirement is rejected or remains incomplete; a complete clean review and an explicitly eligible reduced review succeed.
assurance: schema inspection, runtime verdict guard, exported gate-helper probe
inference: The source/probe establish an accepted omission shape; they do not measure whether a configured reviewer model commonly emits it.

title: Omitted automatic hook setting enables manifest inference despite documented trust opt-in

evidence.detail: autoFileChangeHooks is described as disabled by default and requiring explicit true for trusted projects.
The empty/default configuration leaves autoFileChangeHooks undefined; merging preserves omission.
Only value===false suppresses inference; undefined enters manifest inference.
Rust manifests produce cargo clippy and cargo test commands for changed .rs files.
Real SDK dispatch passes no normalized autoFileChangeHooks choice or explicit hook list.
Public docs promise trusted projects must explicitly set autoFileChangeHooks:true.
Hooks actually default to a bounded 300-second timeout; schema/public no-timeout prose is stale.

trigger: A workspace with Cargo.toml and changed Rust files runs the normal hook gate while autoFileChangeHooks is omitted.
consequence: Manifest-inferred compilers/tests can execute repository-controlled build scripts/test code without the documented trust opt-in. Users also receive conflicting timeout expectations.
suggestedFix: Require config.autoFileChangeHooks===true before inference; use configured hooks otherwise. Inject the effective configuration at the SDK boundary so scope/env choices are explicit. Reconcile documentation and config timeout comments with the selected current timeout contract.
acceptanceProbe: With a harmless captured runner and isolated public config fixture, omitted/false settings run no inferred commands; explicit true selects inferred commands, and explicitly configured hooks still run. Assert the actual default/override timeout sent to the executor.
inference: No untrusted target-project command was executed. Cargo build-script execution is the consequence of the discovered command choice; concrete implicit selection is established statically.
secondaryContractDrift: docs/agents-and-tools.md:113 and provider-config.ts:507 claim unbounded/omitted timeout, while executor forwards hook.timeoutSeconds ?? 300 at file-change-hooks.ts:1605.

title: Targeted validation accepts equal-length untracked tail mutation outside the snapshot byte prefix

evidence.detail: Each changed file contributes at most 1MiB to identity.
Full size plus capped prefix are hashed; equal-length tail changes contribute identical bytes.
The tracked git diff does not contain untracked file contents.
Pre/post source refusal depends on equality of this capped snapshot id.

equalLengthUntrackedTail changes the exported value in a 1,200,028-byte untracked.ts but leaves snapshot unchanged and bundleTruncated:false; midValidationTailMutation returns status:passed and assurance:full after a further tail edit.

trigger: Change a same-length source tail beyond 1MiB in an untracked file, including during targeted validation.
consequence: Distinct source generations alias to one identity, so validation evidence can claim full assurance for bytes that changed mid-run.
suggestedFix: Hash full file contents with incremental bounded I/O, or mark identity incomplete and refuse full/source-bound attestation. Output retention may remain capped independently. Ensure untracked source and capped diff/status tails cannot alias through length-only terms.
acceptanceProbe: Real public bundle changes identity for an equal-length untracked tail edit; the real targeted-validation function rejects the same mid-hook mutation while an unchanged-source successful hook passes. Include large tracked diffs and bounded-memory controls.
assurance: real local Git/SDK integration with injected harmless validation hook
distinctFrom: This is the review/targeted-validation identity path with a 1MiB cap, not the root's native audit inventory 256KB snapshot probe.
inference: No target-project suite or live model review ran; the probe isolates the source identity acceptance guarantee.

title: Review bundles silently drop corrupt unresolved findings after quarantine

evidence.detail: list() returns only records from listWithDiagnostics and discards diagnostics.
Corrupt records are moved into .corrupt with detailed diagnostics.
The real findings consumer uses list(), making corrupted/inaccessible evidence look like an empty list.
The CLI displays finding records only when the returned list is nonempty; no lost-record state is available.
Existing corruption test covers store diagnostics, not bundle propagation.
corruptFindingConsumption: in-scope open finding disappears as findings:[], no error/diagnostic, with its file quarantined.

trigger: A persisted in-scope open finding becomes malformed before get_change_review_bundle reads it.
consequence: Evidence loss is presented as successful empty findings; subsequent reads may be even less diagnostic after quarantine removed the original file.
suggestedFix: Return corruption/availability diagnostics through the review bundle for all evidence kinds and persist a degraded-evidence marker so later calls do not erase the loss state. Distinguish no records, stale/out-of-scope records, and unavailable records.
acceptanceProbe: Seed a current unresolved finding, corrupt it, and require visible degraded/unavailable evidence plus the corruption location on the first and later bundle reads; healthy unrelated records remain available.
inference: The consumer bug does not prove that every default run currently produces LocalHarnessStore finding records; that producer path is itself not established in this slice.

title: Audit completion conflates inspected coverage with feature readiness and cannot certify assessed absence

evidence.detail: Every feature must be verified complete with every implementation category nonempty.
Out-of-scope exclusions apply to structural subsystem coverage, not feature readiness.
The orchestrator must not synthesize until this combined coverage/readiness result is complete.
Canonical flow promotes evidence_kind after exact reads and blocks synthesis on incomplete features.

coverageReadinessSeparation: all inventoried file/domain declarations are valid, known absence is recorded, but complete:false and missing implementation categories remain despite the feature exclusion reason.

trigger: A comprehensive body audit correctly concludes that a requested capability is absent or unwired.
consequence: The audit cannot graduate its inspection while reporting missing product capabilities; it is incentivized to omit a gap or over-promote readiness to satisfy the procedure.
suggestedFix: Separate audit coverage from capability maturity and assurance. Support verified negative evidence and explicit feature dispositions without claiming usability. Keep unknown/uninspected states incomplete.
acceptanceProbe: A source-backed assessed-absent or unwired feature can have coverageComplete:true while readinessComplete:false; an uninspected feature remains coverage-incomplete, and the root's intentionally unimplemented fixture never becomes usable.
assurance: public audit-wrapper probe plus static procedure trace
relationship: Counterpart to the root's existing false-positive completeness probe; consolidate at synthesis if desired, without losing the assessed-absence acceptance requirement.

title: Browser policy defaults and inspection allowlists disagree across production layers

evidence.detail: Schema defaults to allow-interactions
Shared policy restricts only explicit read-only; permits scroll/design_tokens/tab
Shared helper used on outgoing calls
Second narrower list excludes those documented inspection actions
Missing policy is restricted by this handler
Handler test expects default read-only while shared tests expect absent policy allowed

trigger: Spawn bundled browser-use with no interactionPolicy, or explicit read-only/plan-only and request scroll/design_tokens/tab list.
consequence: Omitted policy may be denied despite the schema/prompt default. Read-only inspection actions advertised as supported are denied by the second gate, causing needless respawn/authorization requests and preventing page inspection.
suggestedFix: Choose the intentional default once and share one structural action-policy evaluator across schemas, prompt, executor and handler. Inspect tab operation and recursive diagnose rather than just top-level type.
acceptanceProbe: Drive schema-valid calls through executor plus handler for omitted/read-only/allow-interactions and plan lineage. Omitted matches chosen default; listed inspection actions work; tab create/close and nested mutation remain denied under read-only.
evidenceVsInference: Default application at spawn was not exercised end to end; handler allowlist rejection is unconditional for explicit read-only and is directly evident. Tests encode incompatible contracts.

title: SDK browser dispatch collapses child ownership into the main run session

evidence.detail: Child parentRunId/parentAgentId owner is attached
Trusted owner captures only mainAgentState
Child/model stamp is discarded
Every browser call uses that same main owner
Session key otherwise includes child ownership
Run cleanup selects only clientSessionId
Cleanup also selects every ownerless session

trigger: Two browser-use children in one SDK run issue actions concurrently; separately, one of two SDK runs sharing a client session completes.
consequence: Children resolve to one browser/tab/log state instead of their intended isolated sessions. Main-run cleanup also targets sibling root runs under the same client session and all ownerless sessions, so another task can lose its browser state.
suggestedFix: Carry authenticated per-call child identity as trusted transport context outside model-controlled input while preserving spoof resistance. Scope run cleanup to the exact root run and track explicit ownership for in-flight sessions.
acceptanceProbe: Two browser children in a fake SDK dispatch must receive distinct session keys. Two root runs under one client ID must survive the other's completion; spoofed owner input must still be rejected.
evidenceVsInference: Identity replacement/key derivation/cleanup predicates are static evidence. Cross-task navigation or teardown interference is a consequence inferred for concurrent callers; no live browser race was executed.
crossReferences: pair09 owns shared job/run/process lifecycle; this finding concerns browser target/observation ownership

title: Diagnose discards step media and returns no verdict for declared success conditions

evidence.detail: Schema advertises success conditions to verify
Step output is reduced to the first JSON part
Expected logs/error/custom conditions are copied only
Outer response uses ordinary success:true builder

trigger: Run diagnose with a screenshot/recording/diff step, a failed action, or expectedLogs/noJsErrors/customCondition expectations.
consequence: A step can say screenshotAttached:true while no image reaches the model, and callers receive requested conditions without an evaluated verdict. Nested failures remain inspectable in JSON, but outer success is only sequence dispatch completion.
suggestedFix: Preserve/reference step media with step IDs, return evaluated condition results and an explicit aggregate outcome, and distinguish action execution from validation. Reject unsupported condition types.
acceptanceProbe: Offline fake-CDP screenshot plus failed evaluate reproduces current outer success:true, screenshotAttached:true and zero media. Corrected path must deliver/reference the screenshot and expose failed/unsupported condition verdicts.
evidenceVsInference: Fake-CDP probe directly confirms media loss and outer/nested statuses. Non-evaluation of condition fields is static evidence.

title: Pixel diff silently excludes non-overlapping image area from mismatch ratio

evidence.detail: Comparison uses min width/height
Both PNGs cropped to that intersection
Mismatch ratio denominator covers intersection only
Original dimensions exposed, but no partial/dimension-mismatch verdict

trigger: Compare images with identical shared pixels but different viewport/page extents.
consequence: MismatchRatio can be 0 despite missing/extra page area. Original dimensions are returned, so a caller could detect it independently; the primary diff statistic is incomplete without an explicit crop/dimension result.
suggestedFix: Default unequal dimensions to an explicit dimension mismatch, or compare a padded union; make overlap-only comparison opt-in and mark it partial.
acceptanceProbe: The offline 2x1 versus 1x1 fixture currently gives 0 mismatch across one pixel despite a differing second pixel. Corrected default must expose nonzero/dimension mismatch; an explicit overlap mode must disclose ignored extent.
evidenceVsInference: Direct fixture execution of the production pixel_diff dispatcher; no website or private image involved.

title: Native-inspectable glTF, GLB and OBJ assets cannot use the advertised preview importer

evidence.detail: Discovery includes blend/glb/gltf/fbx/obj/dae/3ds/etc
Preview advertises supported 3D assets imported through fixed operators
Fixed importer contains only fbx/dae/stl/ply/USD branches
All other formats raise importer unavailable
All non-blend previews use that importer

trigger: Call render_3d_preview on a successfully native-inspected .gltf/.glb/.obj, or inspect/preview a discovered .3ds.
consequence: The fixed Python script necessarily rejects these formats even with Blender installed; discovery/read support does not constitute preview support.
suggestedFix: Add tested glTF/GLB and OBJ operators for supported Blender versions. Return an explicit per-format/per-operation capability packet; mark 3ds unavailable unless a supported importer exists.
acceptanceProbe: Fixture suite must inspect and preview one glTF, GLB and OBJ on the declared Blender version and negotiate unavailable formats before creating artifacts. Missing Blender/operator must return truthful unsupported/error states.
evidenceVsInference: Missing branches and unconditional ValueError are static evidence. Actual installed Blender was not launched, and no importer/version compatibility was measured.

title: Preview receipts do not guarantee the exact source bytes or dimensions claimed

evidence.detail: Source bytes/hash captured in an initial filesystem read
Blender later reopens the original live path
Imported formats also receive the live source path
Receipt sourceHash is reused from initial read
Dimensions copied from requested parameters, not decoded PNG
Docs promise exact source hash used for rendering

trigger: Editor replaces a source asset between initial hash/read and Blender opening it; Blender produces an image whose dimensions differ from the request.
consequence: The receipt can bind the produced preview to an earlier asset revision or requested dimensions that were never observed. Metadata caching for Blender inspection has the same hash-before-reopen gap.
suggestedFix: Render/inspect a verified immutable source snapshot, preserve/remap relative dependencies or label their limits, and decode output PNG dimensions. Bind model media to the same artifact bytes/hash and report stale/limited evidence when exact binding is unavailable.
acceptanceProbe: An injected source replacement between read and process open must render the initial snapshot or return stale evidence. Decode and hash the exact returned PNG; wrong dimensions or changed artifact bytes must never retain an exact receipt claim.
evidenceVsInference: Hashing, later path reopen and receipt construction are static evidence. The wrong-revision outcome is an inference conditional on that explicit concurrent replacement; no actual Blender race or malformed-render output was executed.

title: Applied 3D edits report previewRendered true for preview error JSON

evidence.detail: Preview failure returns a JSON {error} part
Applied edit calls post-commit preview with the same signal
Any JSON part selected, including error
previewRendered is only JSON-part existence
Conditional Blender test asserts only successful preview case

trigger: Guarded edit commits, then preview is cancelled, Blender fails, or no image is available.
consequence: Applied mutation truth is preserved, and preview.error is exposed, but previewRendered contradicts it by remaining true. Clients using this boolean can wrongly credit visual verification.
suggestedFix: Set previewRendered from validated successful image receipts/media, not JSON existence; distinguish rendered-but-not-attached, failed and cancelled states without changing the applied edit outcome.
acceptanceProbe: Fake subprocess/DI fixture commits then returns a preview error or abort. Require outcome:applied, retained artifactPath, explicit preview error and previewRendered:false. Cover rendered-but-filtered media separately.
evidenceVsInference: Error-return shape and boolean test are static evidence; the combined commit-then-preview-failure path was not executed in this audit.

title: Failed image retries still send the retained old capture as current message media

evidence.detail: Failed retry keeps previous capture while setting error
Processed bytes projected regardless of attachment status
Comment/contract says processing/error images should not be sent
Production message preparation uses this helper
Returned media passed as SDK content

trigger: A ready image loses its source, retry fails, and the user submits the draft/queued prompt.
consequence: UI/error state describes a failed capture, while the model receives retained previous bytes without a retained/stale indicator. The output can be based on an observation the user intended to refresh.
suggestedFix: Gate media projection on ready status. Preserve old bytes for inspection, and support an explicit reuse-retained-capture action that marks provenance/time rather than silently sending it.
acceptanceProbe: Actual retryPendingAttachment plus processImagesForMessage in the offline fixture currently yields status:error and one image part. Corrected preparation must reject/omit that capture with a visible message or require explicit retained reuse.
evidenceVsInference: Direct production-helper fixture verifies the failed retry and emitted image part; full mounted CLI submit was not exercised.

title: render_ui claims rendering without a host capability or acknowledgement

evidence.detail: Returns UI rendered without consulting host or tool input
Tool contract describes CLI rendering
The concrete renderer is CLI-specific
Unsupported widget can yield no rendered content

trigger: An SDK/headless host exposes render_ui without the Openbuff CLI consumer, or a UI render fails after the runtime acknowledges.
consequence: Model receives UI rendered even when no widget was rendered. The working CLI button does not establish a render contract on other hosts.
suggestedFix: Report widget submission with host delivery state, expose/render only where host capability is negotiated, and acknowledge rendering separately if a client needs that guarantee.
acceptanceProbe: Headless SDK host with no UI handler must report unsupported/not-rendered or submitted without a render guarantee. Mounted CLI path should acknowledge the actual supported button while preserving open/copy failure behavior.
evidenceVsInference: Unconditional handler response and concrete CLI registry are static evidence; full headless model task and rendering failure were not executed.
